name: Eggplant
tile_uses: House flavor base, rice bowls, pasta, sides
why_now: Eggplant peaks in late summer — August is when Southern California farms produce them in abundance. The flesh is less bitter than in off-season months, and the skin is thinner. What arrives now roasts into something deeply savory with minimal effort.
how_to_choose: Firm with no soft spots — a soft eggplant will be bitter and seedy
Glossy, taut skin rather than dull or wrinkled
Lighter weight for its size often means fewer seeds
The cap and stem should still look fresh, not dry
buy_this_much: 1 large eggplant or 2 small ones for the week.
price_note: Eggplant is inexpensive in August when supply peaks. Italian eggplant (the long, narrow variety) and Japanese eggplant roast particularly well.

flavor_paths.name: Roasted high and hot
flavor_paths.description: Cut into chunks, high heat, left alone. It collapses into something sweet and savory.

flavor_paths.name: Charred whole
flavor_paths.description: Over an open flame or under a broiler until the skin is completely black. Scoop out the smoky flesh.

flavor_paths.name: Pan-fried
flavor_paths.description: Sliced thick, olive oil, high heat. Leave it alone until it releases from the pan.

weekday_uses: Roasted in chunks and added to a rice bowl
Pan-fried thick slices alongside chicken or fish
Folded into pasta with cherry tomatoes and basil
weekend_use: Charred whole over flame or under the broiler, flesh scooped out and mixed with olive oil, garlic, and lemon. Serve with bread.
storage: Counter for a day or two, then refrigerator. Don't buy it more than three or four days before you plan to use it.
one_thing_to_learn: You don't need to salt modern eggplant. The salting-and-draining method was developed for older, bitter varieties. Current cultivars have had the bitterness bred out. What actually matters is heat — a crowded pan steams and makes it soggy. Give the pieces room, use a hot pan, and leave them alone until they release and color.
market_question: What variety is this? Italian or Japanese?
